title: Relationship of Ferritin and Procalcitonin with (SOFA)-2 Scores in Intensive Care Patients with COVID-19-Associated Sepsis and Their  Prognostic Value
content: Background/Objectives: To our knowledge, this is the first study to simultaneously investigate the prognostic value of serum ferritin and procalcitonin (PCT) in relation to (SOFA)-2 score-based organ dysfunction severity in intensive care patients diagnosed with COVID-19-associated sepsis. Methods: Patients were stratified based on day 5 ferritin (ng/mL) and PCT levels (μg/L). Prognostic performance was analysed across severity groups defined by (SOFA)-2 score of &lt;5 (mild) and ≥5 (severe). Results: Day 5 PCT levels did not significantly predict (SOFA)-2 score (p &gt; 0.05). The optimal day 5 ferritin cut-off was &gt;1,191 ng/mL, with 35.78% sensitivity and 82.38% specificity (AUC = 0.608). Elevated ferritin levels may help identify patients at higher risk of adverse outcomes who may benefit from closer monitoring or intensive care escalation. By contrast, PCT did not provide additional predictive value for organ dysfunction severity in COVID-19 beyond existing inflammatory markers, consistent with its known suppression during primary viral infections. Conclusions: Serum ferritin showed a significant positive association with (SOFA)-2 score, supporting its role as a clinically relevant biomarker for disease stratification in COVID-19-associated sepsis. These findings may extend to non-COVID sepsis populations where macrophage activation and iron dysregulation drive organ dysfunction.
